question.text: An exporter buys 200 lots of USDINR 84.00 put at Rs. 0.25 to hedge USD 200,000. At expiry, USDINR is 83.00. Effective realization rate?

explanation.text: The Logic: A protective put gives the exporter a floor realisation equal to Strike - Premium. With strike 84.00 and premium Rs. 0.25, the floor = 84.00 - 0.25 = Rs. 83.75. Equivalently, at expiry USDINR is 83.00, so the exporter exercises the put: spot sale 83.00 + put payoff 1.00 - premium 0.25 = Rs. 83.75 per USD. The Trap: Option B (Rs. 84.00) is the strike and ignores premium paid. Option C (Rs. 83.00) is the unhedged spot realisation. Option D (Rs. 84.25) wrongly adds the premium to the strike. Note: Distributor-specific and cross-exam framing removed; explanation kept to neutral protective-put floor-rate wording (Strike - Premium).
